covariant-derivative-in-quantum-chromody.title: Covariant Derivative in Quantum Chromodynamics
covariant-derivative-in-quantum-chromody.conceptual_definition: The covariant derivative $D_\mu$ in Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) is an operator that replaces the ordinary partial derivative $\partial_\mu$ to ensure that the Lagrangian density of matter fields remains invariant under local $SU(3)$ gauge transformations.
covariant-derivative-in-quantum-chromody.intuitive_summary: It modifies the standard derivative to account for the 'color charge' of quarks and gluons, allowing them to interact via the strong force while maintaining the fundamental symmetry of the theory.
covariant-derivative-in-quantum-chromody.interpretation: In quantum field theories, particularly non-abelian gauge theories like QCD, fields transform locally under a gauge group. To construct a Lagrangian that is invariant under these local transformations, the ordinary partial derivative must be replaced by a covariant derivative. This derivative introduces a coupling to the gauge fields ($G_\mu^a$, the gluons in QCD), which mediate the strong force. The term $i$ g_s T^a G_$\mu$^a$ represents this interaction, where $g_s$ is the strong coupling constant, and $T^a$ are the generators of the $SU(3)$ color group, acting on the color indices of the quark fields. The summation over the color index $a$ is implicit. This ensures that when a field undergoes a local gauge transformation, its derivative also transforms appropriately, preserving the form of the Lagrangian.
covariant-derivative-in-quantum-chromody.symmetry_origin: The covariant derivative is a direct consequence of demanding local $SU(3)$ gauge symmetry for the quark fields. Under a local gauge transformation $\Psi(x) \rightarrow U(x) \Psi(x)$, where $U(x) = e^{i g_s \theta^a(x) T^a}$, the ordinary derivative $\partial_\mu \Psi(x)$ does not transform covariantly. The covariant derivative $D_\mu \Psi(x)$ is constructed precisely so that it transforms in the same way as the field itself, i.e., $D_\mu \Psi(x) \rightarrow U(x) (D_\mu \Psi(x))$. This requirement introduces the gauge field $G_\mu^a$ and its interaction term, which is essential for the consistency of the theory and leads to the existence of the strong force.
covariant-derivative-in-quantum-chromody.limits_and_boundary: In the limit where the strong coupling constant $g_s \rightarrow 0$, or in the absence of any gluon fields ($G_\mu^a = 0$), the covariant derivative reduces to the ordinary partial derivative, $D_\mu \rightarrow \partial_\mu$. This corresponds to a free theory without strong interactions. Conversely, in the deep ultraviolet (high energy) regime, $g_s$ becomes small due to asymptotic freedom, and the interaction term becomes weaker, approaching a free theory.

D_mu.name: Covariant Derivative Operator
D_mu.description: The operator that replaces the ordinary partial derivative in gauge theories to ensure local gauge invariance. It acts on fields that transform under the $SU(3)$ gauge group.

partial_mu.name: Ordinary Partial Derivative Operator
partial_mu.description: The standard partial derivative with respect to the spacetime coordinate $x^\mu$.

i.name: Imaginary Unit
i.description: The imaginary unit, $\sqrt{-1}$, characteristic of quantum mechanical operators.

g_s.name: Strong Coupling Constant
g_s.description: The dimensionless coupling constant that determines the strength of the strong interaction in Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD).

T_a.name: Generators of SU(3) Gauge Group
T_a.description: A set of eight $3 \times 3$ Hermitian, traceless matrices (Gell-Mann matrices) that are the generators of the $SU(3)$ color gauge group, representing the color charges.

G_mu_a.name: Gluon Field
G_mu_a.description: The components of the gluon field, which is the gauge field mediating the strong force. The index $\mu$ is a Lorentz index, and $a$ is a color index ($a=1, \dots, 8$). It is a vector potential for the strong force.
